title: Democracy is a scam and I can prove it
summary: An Educated Barbarian episode in which NH uses Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil to argue that equality is a social construct, and that democracy breeds mediocrity, hostility to excellence and dissolved responsibility. He argues this makes a herd that welcomes authoritarianism. He ends by urging individuals to keep their independence and will rather than wait for the system to save them.
claims: The Educated Barbarian philosophy series returns as rarer, much longer videos so the channel stays mostly bodybuilding; frequent philosophy uploads hurt channel growth
Equality is a social construct: nobody is born equal and it needs legal enforcement to exist, which does not by itself make it bad
Humans rose above nature by repeatedly defying it; 'equality is a false god' memes miss that social constructs are a necessary evil
The danger is forgetting that equality is man-made and treating it as natural; then it starts controlling us
Rousseau's noble-savage view is wrong; war is the natural state of man and society is a precious, fragile construct needing constant vigilance (Nietzsche's view)
Democracy breeds hatred of excellence: anyone rising above the masses becomes a threat, so it favours the temperate average over the outlier
Democracy is only ever defended by comparison with worse systems, never justified on its own merits
Democracy multiplies the herd instinct of obedience because following is safe and needs no skill, while the commanding instinct withers
Under equality everyone gets to be comfortable but no one gets to be great; chasing pleasure and dodging pain makes men mediocre
Democracy dissolves responsibility: politicians blame voters, voters protest leaders they elected, and voting outsources personal responsibility
The COVID era showed people readily trade others' freedom for their own security; they value their own freedom, not freedom in general
People present selfish desires as the 'common good', which lets governments take more power
The welfare state punishes excellence and keeps the poor dependent by removing their incentive to improve, removing responsibility from rich and poor and benefiting only the state
Modern justice grows lenient toward criminals while treating critics of the system as the real danger
Past kings waged war honestly by power; democracies justify the same bloodshed under moral pretexts
Don't wait for the system to save you: resist values that sap your strength and rely on your own will
